mutations.description: Delete every customer row instead of deduplicating.
Invert the id comparison and keep the highest id per email group.
mutations.sql:
DELETE FROM customers
WHERE EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM customers AS keeper
    WHERE keeper.email IS customers.email COLLATE BINARY
      AND keeper.id > customers.id
);

mutations.description: Treat created_at as the retention rule and keep the earliest timestamp. The nonsequential fixture has an earlier timestamp on a higher id.
mutations.sql:
DELETE FROM customers
WHERE EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM customers AS keeper
    WHERE keeper.email IS customers.email COLLATE BINARY
      AND keeper.created_at < customers.created_at
);

mutations.description: Use plain equality instead of NULL-safe IS, so the NULL duplicate group is never deduplicated.
mutations.sql:
DELETE FROM customers
WHERE EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM customers AS keeper
    WHERE keeper.email = customers.email COLLATE BINARY
      AND keeper.id < customers.id
);

mutations.description: Collapse case and surrounding whitespace before comparing emails, which is not the declared exact BINARY rule.
mutations.sql:
DELETE FROM customers
WHERE EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM customers AS keeper
    WHERE keeper.email IS NOT NULL
      AND customers.email IS NOT NULL
      AND lower(trim(keeper.email)) = lower(trim(customers.email))
      AND keeper.id < customers.id
);

mutations.description: Delete only the highest-id row among all duplicated emails, leaving every other duplicate in place.
mutations.sql:
DELETE FROM customers
WHERE id = (
    SELECT MAX(candidate.id)
    FROM customers AS candidate
    WHERE EXISTS (
        SELECT 1
        FROM customers AS other
        WHERE other.email IS candidate.email COLLATE BINARY
          AND other.id <> candidate.id
    )
);

mutations.description: Apply the correct customer deduplication but also delete the unrelated table. The unrelated rows prove collateral writes are graded.

references.description: Delete every row that has a lower-id row in the same exact BINARY email group. IS keeps NULL as one group.
references.sql:
DELETE FROM customers
WHERE EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM customers AS keeper
    WHERE keeper.email IS customers.email COLLATE BINARY
      AND keeper.id < customers.id
);

references.description: Group by the email column (BINARY collation) and keep the minimum numeric id in each group, including the NULL group.
Rank rows within each email group by id and delete every rank above one. This is a window-function alternative to the grouped MIN formulation.

retentionRule.idempotency: Applying a correct deduplication statement twice must leave the same once-correct final state.
retentionRule.statement: Keep the row with the lowest numeric id for each exact email value. NULL is one duplicate group. Case, leading/trailing whitespace and inner whitespace are significant. Unrelated tables must be unchanged.
retentionRule.tieBreaker: not applicable: id is the unique integer primary key
